name: Mueller Water Products
headline: Fire hydrants and valves that cities specify and rarely switch away from.
what_short: Fire hydrants, valves and water-system products
what_it_does: Mueller Water Products makes iron gate valves, specialty valves, fire hydrants, meters and leak-detection and pressure-management products for water systems. It sells through waterworks distributors. About 60% to 65% of its $1.43 billion of sales goes to repairing and replacing city water systems.
why_it_passed: Cities approve a limited number of hydrant brands so they can use the same tools and spare parts, and its hydrants and gate valves are specified in the 100 largest US metropolitan areas.
It held its prices through the 2009 downturn.
It earned 40.5% a year before tax on the tangible capital it needs in fiscal 2025 (about 25% counting goodwill and intangibles still on its books).
Its principal competitors are two private companies, McWane and American Cast Iron Pipe, in a heavy, bulky product that is costly to import.
why_not_now: At $22.02 a share the price is above the top of the analysis's value range of $10.73 to $16.76. The cash the business produces is 2.7% of the price on a five-year average, against 5.63% on a 30-year US Treasury bond. The analysis's fair price is $7.47.
watch: It owes an environmental indemnity of undetermined size to the buyer of its former U.S. Pipe business (the North Birmingham Superfund site).
Two distributors account for 37% of gross sales.
It has a history of past acquisitions that were later written off, and its recent buybacks were made at prices above the analysis's value range.
A 2021 fatal accident at its Albertville plant was noted in the analysis.
